statement.p: Suppose that z is a linear function of x and y with slope 3 in the x direction and slope -2 in the y direction.
(a) A change of -0.1 in x and 0.2 in y produces what change in z?
(b) If z=4 when x=3 and y=4, what is the value of z when x=2.8 and y=4.2?

static.solution:
(a) Since z is a linear function of x and y with slope 3 in the x direction, and slope -2 in the y direction, we have: z = 3 x - 2 y + c. We can write an equation for changes in z in terms of changes in x and y: \Delta z = (3 (x + \Delta x) - 2(y + \Delta y) + c) - (3 x - 2 y + c) = 3 \Delta x - 2 \Delta y. Since \Delta x = -0.1 and \Delta y = 0.2, we have \Delta z = 3 (-0.1) - 2(0.2) = -0.7. So a -0.1 change in x and a 0.2 change in y produces a -0.7 change in z.
(b) As we know that z=4 when x=3 and y=4, the value of z when x=2.8 and y=4.2 will be z = 4 + \Delta z = 4 + 3\Delta x - 2\Delta y. where \Delta z is the change in z when x changes from 3 to 2.8 and y changes from 4 to 4.2. We have \Delta x = 2.8 - 3 = -0.2 and \Delta y = 4.2 - 4 = 0.2. Therefore, when x=2.8 and y=4.2, we have z = 4 + 3 \cdot(-0.2) - 2\cdot(0.2) = 3.
